record.paper_title: A Proximal Quasi-Newton Trust-Region Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
record.original_question: For nonsmooth regularized optimization problems of the form minimize f(x) + h(x), where f is continuously differentiable and h is proper, lower semicontinuous, and may be nonconvex, can the convergence analysis of the proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method be generalized to allow unbounded Hessian or quasi-Newton approximations when those approximations do not deteriorate too fast?

evidence.quote: Hessian approximations are unbounded, provided they do not deteriorate too fast
It may be possible to generalize our analysis along similar lines.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nonsmooth regularized optimization problem
    minimize over x in R^n   F(x) := f(x) + h(x),
where f : R^n → R is continuously differentiable (with, in standard assumptions, locally Lipschitz-continuous gradient) and h : R^n → R ∪ {+∞} is proper and lower semicontinuous, possibly nonconvex.

A proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method generates iterates x_k by approximately minimizing, within a trust region of radius Δ_k, a model of the form
    m_k(s) = f(x_k) + ⟨∇f(x_k), s⟩ + (1/2) ⟨s, B_k s⟩ + h(x_k + s),
where B_k is a symmetric Hessian or quasi-Newton approximation (e.g., PSB, BFGS, SR1). Standard convergence analyses assume that the family {B_k} is uniformly bounded, i.e., sup_k ‖B_k‖ < ∞, and prove that a suitable first-order stationarity measure tends to zero.

Question: Can the global convergence analysis of such a proximal quasi-Newton trust-region method be extended to allow the sequence {‖B_k‖} to be unbounded, provided the approximations do not deteriorate too fast — for instance, under a controlled growth condition of the form ‖B_k‖ ≤ C (1 + |S_k|)^p for some constants C > 0 and p ∈ [0, 1), where S_k denotes the index set of successful iterations up to iteration k — and still guarantee convergence of a first-order stationarity measure to zero, together with a worst-case iteration complexity bound for reaching ε-approximate stationarity?
artifact.status_search_result: Follow-up work has carried out exactly this generalization. Two recent papers in Mathematical Programming establish complexity and convergence results for trust-region methods with potentially unbounded model Hessians, including the nonsmooth regularized setting. They prove convergence of a first-order stationarity measure to zero and a worst-case complexity bound of O(ε^(-2/(1-p))) when the model Hessians grow no faster than |S_k|^p with 0 ≤ p < 1, matching the controlled-deterioration condition envisioned. This indicates the question has been answered affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of trust-region methods with potentially unbounded Hessian approximations for smooth and nonsmooth optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Trust-region methods for the sum of a smooth term and a nonsmooth term, with model Hessians allowed to be unbounded, achieve global convergence and O(1/ε^{2/(1-p)}) complexity.
status_evidence.claim: The convergence analysis has been extended to nonsmooth regularized problems with unbounded model Hessians whose growth is controlled by |S_k|^p, p in [0,1).

status_evidence.title: Complexity of trust-region methods in the presence of unbounded Hessian approximations
status_evidence.snippet: Tight worst-case complexity O(1/ε^{2/(1-p)}) is established when model Hessians may diverge no faster than |S_k|^p.
status_evidence.claim: Controlled-growth unbounded Hessian approximations are compatible with global convergence and explicit complexity bounds in trust-region methods.

status_evidence.title: A Proximal Modified Quasi-Newton Method for Nonsmooth Regularized Optimization
status_evidence.snippet: Proximal quasi-Newton method for f+h with relaxed boundedness assumptions on quasi-Newton matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent proximal quasi-Newton work for nonsmooth regularized problems relaxes uniform boundedness of the quasi-Newton approximations.
